| [CLAIM-266](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-266.md) v2 | A family of probes that supplies an optimized system's training signal cannot also certify what the system preserves: optimization pushes toward whatever the probes reward, including what they cannot see, so preservation must be shown under probes not used to train it | The general content of [CLAIM-149](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-149.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that it does not rest on [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md)'s account of correspondences in translation. | [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) v2 | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity".
